newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares lose ground, BUX futures tumble.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares lose ground, BUX futures tumble.

text.p: Hungarian share prices dropped one percent on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Thursday following a 1.42 percent fall on Wall Street and traders said domestic buyers saved the market from a bigger decline.
The BUX index closed at 5,301.15 points, down 52.34.
Indicative indices provided by the bourse showed that the BUX opened at 5,289.58 points, bottomed out at 5,281.89 points and closed at the day's high of 5,301.15.
"Major shareholders were not frightened and they prefer to hold," said Peter Lencs of MKB Securities. "There are hardly any new buyers, this is reflected by the turnover."
Spot share turnover totalled 1.69 billion forints.

Domestic demand seemed to absorb the slightly increasing supply, Lencs said, adding that there were still not too many sellers on the bourse. "There aren't sale orders without price limits on the market."
On Thursday main losers of the market included hotelier Danubius which fell 250 forints to 5,050,
Chemicals Borsodchem which raised capital in its two subsidiaries, fell 110 foints to 6,110, while the other chemical paper, TVK dropped 30 forints to 2,270.
Analysts in London said the market's near term future will be influenced by two conflicting factors.
"Investors increasingly think the Fed's hike was the first step in a series...and this drives Wall Street lower," said Gabor Sitanyi, analyst at ING Barings in London.

"On the other hand investors sold a lot, not only in Hungary, not only in the region but practically everywhere... this means that many funds are sitting on cash equivalent to as much as 30 percent (of the portfolio)," he said.
"This is encouraging...as they have to spend it sometime."
Share offers in oil and gas company MOL and in pharamceuticals Richter are expected in May.
